quests.hint: Explain a decision by giving your criteria and the benefit. 'Because' should carry the weight.
quests.explanation: A clear decision explanation names what you compared and what you gained. Connecting the savings to a concrete use (the training program) makes the choice feel purposeful.
quests.situationText: Your team is asking why you chose the cheaper supplier. The quality difference was small, and the savings will pay for a training program.
quests.sampleAnswer: I chose the cheaper supplier because the quality difference was small, and the savings will fund the training program.
quests.correctAnswer: I went with the cheaper supplier because the quality difference was small, and the savings will pay for the training program.
acceptedSynonyms: The cheaper supplier made sense to me, since there's little difference in quality, and the money saved will fund training.
My reasoning was simple. Quality was nearly the same, and the savings will cover our training program.
I picked the cheaper option because we lose very little in quality, and we gain enough to finance the training program.
I went with the cheaper supplier because the quality difference was small, and the savings will pay for the training program.

quests.hint: When a decision disappoints some people, acknowledge their preference and explain the trade-off.
quests.explanation: Recognizing that some wanted an earlier date shows respect. Explaining the cost of the alternative ('a rushed launch would cost us more') helps them understand, even if they still disagree.
quests.situationText: Some colleagues wanted to launch in January, but you chose March. You're explaining your decision at a team meeting.
quests.sampleAnswer: I know some of you wanted the earlier date. I decided on March because we need time for testing, and a rushed launch would cost us more.
quests.correctAnswer: I know some of you wanted an earlier date. I chose March because we need time to test, and a rushed launch would cost us more in the end.
acceptedSynonyms: I realize several of you hoped for January. I went with March because we need proper testing, and rushing would be more expensive.
I know some of you wanted an earlier date. I chose March because we need time to test, and a rushed launch would cost us more in the end.
I understand the wish for an earlier launch. March gives us time for testing, and launching in a hurry would cost more later.
I know it's not what everyone wanted. March allows for testing, and a hasty launch would end up costing us more.

quests.hint: A personal decision needs no defense, but a brief honest reason helps people understand it.
quests.explanation: Sharing a value-based reason ('I want to be at home') is more convincing than saying 'it's not right for me'. Stating the decision first avoids sounding uncertain.
quests.situationText: You've decided to turn down a promotion that would involve traveling half the year. A close colleague asks why.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've decided to turn down the promotion. It would mean traveling half the year, and I want to be at home with my family.
quests.correctAnswer: I've decided not to accept the promotion. It would mean traveling for half the year, and I want to be at home with my family.
acceptedSynonyms: I'm turning down the promotion. The travel would take me away for six months of the year, and my family matters more to me.
I said no to the promotion, because half the year on the road wouldn't work with the time I want at home.
I've chosen to decline it. Being away half the year isn't compatible with what I want for my family.
I've decided not to accept the promotion. It would mean traveling for half the year, and I want to be at home with my family.

quests.hint: Own the mistake, fix it, and describe the change that stops it happening again. Three steps, no excuses.
quests.explanation: The strongest apology names the mistake, shows it's already corrected, and gives a specific prevention step. Vague promises to 'be more careful' don't have the same weight.
quests.situationText: You sent a client the wrong file by email. They've just pointed it out. You want to respond professionally.
quests.sampleAnswer: I apologize, that's my error. The right file is on its way, and I'm going to check all attachments twice in future.
quests.correctAnswer: That was my mistake. I sent the wrong file. I've just sent the correct one, and I'll double-check attachments from now on.
acceptedSynonyms: I apologize, that's my error. The right file is on its way, and I'm going to check all attachments twice in future.
That was my mistake. I sent the wrong file. I've just sent the correct one, and I'll double-check attachments from now on.
I made a mistake with the attachment. I've sent the correct one, and I'll be verifying every file before sending.
The wrong file went out because of me. The correct one is now in your inbox, and I've changed how I check attachments.

quests.hint: Own a planning error to a manager by naming the mistake, admitting you should have raised it earlier, and offering a new plan.
quests.explanation: 'I should have told you sooner' recognizes the second mistake (late reporting), which managers care about greatly. Bringing a new schedule proves you're focused on solutions.
quests.situationText: You underestimated how long testing would take, and you've now realized the project will be late. You didn't mention the risk earlier. You speak to your manager.
quests.sampleAnswer: I underestimated how long testing would take, and I should have told you sooner. Here's the new schedule, and here's how I'll prevent it happening again.
quests.correctAnswer: I underestimated how long testing would take, and I should have told you earlier. Here's the revised schedule, and here's how I'll prevent it in future.
acceptedSynonyms: I got the testing time wrong, and I should have warned you sooner. I've prepared a new schedule and a way to avoid this next time.
That's on me. I misjudged the testing, and I should have raised it earlier. This is the updated plan, and this is how I'll stop it recurring.
I underestimated the testing phase and I'm sorry I didn't tell you earlier. I've brought a new timeline and some changes to prevent it happening again.
I underestimated how long testing would take, and I should have told you earlier. Here's the revised schedule, and here's how I'll prevent it in future.

quests.hint: When the company is responsible, say so plainly, and offer a concrete remedy with a date. Avoid passive phrases like 'mistakes were made'.
quests.explanation: 'We got this wrong' is direct and human. A remedy with a delivery date is how the customer sees your promise become real.
quests.situationText: As a customer service manager, you've discovered that your company sent a customer the wrong item. You call her to resolve it. The replacement will arrive by Friday.
quests.sampleAnswer: That's our mistake, and I apologize. We'll pay for a replacement, and I'll personally make sure it arrives by Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: We got this wrong, and I'm sorry. We'll cover the cost of the replacement and make sure it reaches you by Friday.
acceptedSynonyms: That's our mistake, and I apologize. We'll pay for a replacement, and I'll personally make sure it arrives by Friday.
We got this wrong, and I'm sorry. We'll cover the cost of the replacement and make sure it reaches you by Friday.
I'm sorry, the error was ours. A replacement will be sent at our cost and delivered by Friday.
We made a mistake, and I take responsibility for it. The replacement will cost you nothing and will be with you by Friday.

quests.hint: Buy thinking time with a phrase that acknowledges the question. Silence feels longer to you than to the audience.
quests.explanation: Phrases like 'That's an important point' give you a few seconds to think while making the questioner feel heard. Adding a sentence about how you'll answer helps organize your response.
quests.situationText: During a live Q&A with senior managers, someone asks a difficult question and you need a moment to organize your thoughts.
quests.sampleAnswer: That's an important point. Let me think about how best to answer it.
quests.correctAnswer: That's an important question. Let me think for a moment about how best to answer it.
acceptedSynonyms: That's an important question. Let me think for a moment about how best to answer it.
Good question. I'd like a second to organize my thoughts.
That deserves a careful answer. Give me a moment to think it through.
I'm glad you raised that. Let me consider the best way to answer.

quests.hint: If you haven't understood, offer two possible interpretations before you answer. It prevents a wrong answer.
quests.explanation: Asking which of two things they mean shows you're taking the question seriously, and it narrows the scope. It's better than answering a question that wasn't asked.
quests.situationText: In a meeting, a director asks, 'How does this affect us?' You aren't sure whether he means the cost or the timeline.
quests.sampleAnswer: Just to make sure I answer the right question, are you asking about the cost or the timeline?
quests.correctAnswer: Just so I answer the right question, do you mean the effect on cost or on the timeline?
acceptedSynonyms: Could I check what you mean? Is your question about the expense or about the schedule?
Do you want me to talk about the impact on the budget or on the deadline? I'd like to answer properly.
Just so I answer the right question, do you mean the effect on cost or on the timeline?
Before I respond, could you clarify whether you're asking about costs or timing?

quests.hint: Disagree in public by stating your view, referring to evidence, and offering to share it privately. It avoids a public argument.
quests.explanation: Saying 'I see it differently' respectfully signals disagreement. Offering the numbers 'after the meeting' avoids a long debate in front of everyone while showing that you have evidence.
quests.situationText: During a meeting, a colleague says sales fell last quarter. According to your figures, they actually rose. You don't want to embarrass him in front of others.
quests.sampleAnswer: That doesn't match what I've seen. The data points the other way, so could we compare notes after the meeting?
quests.correctAnswer: I see that differently. The figures from last quarter suggest the opposite, and I'm happy to share them after the meeting.
acceptedSynonyms: I see that differently. The figures from last quarter suggest the opposite, and I'm happy to share them after the meeting.
I have a different view. My figures show an increase last quarter, and I'd be glad to go through them with you afterwards.
I'm reading the numbers differently. They indicate that sales went up, and I can show you after we finish.
That doesn't match what I've seen. The data points the other way, so could we compare notes after the meeting?

quests.hint: Deliver disappointing news early in the message, then immediately present an alternative. It softens the blow.
quests.explanation: Warning the customer ('disappointing news') and quickly offering the newer model at the same price shows that you're thinking about their needs. The problem and solution come in one breath.
quests.situationText: You work in a shop. A customer ordered a product that has been discontinued, and you want to offer the newer model at the same price.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm afraid I have some disappointing news. The item you ordered has been discontinued. I'd like to offer you the newer model at the same price.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid I have some disappointing news. The item you ordered has been discontinued, but I can offer you the newer model at the same price.
acceptedSynonyms: Unfortunately, the product you ordered is no longer made. However, I can give you the updated model for the same price.
I'm afraid I have some disappointing news. The item you ordered has been discontinued, but I can offer you the newer model at the same price.
I'm sorry to say your item has been discontinued. What I can do is offer the newer version at the price you were quoted.
I have to tell you that the item is discontinued. To make up for it, I could offer the latest model at the original price.

quests.hint: Apologize, give the reason briefly, and offer two real alternatives.
quests.explanation: Offering a specific date and a cancellation list gives the patient two ways to move forward. The reason ('the specialist is ill') is shared briefly, without unnecessary detail.
quests.situationText: You're a clinic receptionist and must cancel a patient's appointment because the specialist is ill. The next slot is Monday.
quests.sampleAnswer: We've had to cancel your appointment because the specialist is ill. I'm very sorry. I can offer you a slot next Monday, or put you on a cancellation list.
quests.correctAnswer: We've had to cancel your appointment because the specialist is unwell. I'm very sorry. I can offer you next Monday, or add you to a cancellation list.
acceptedSynonyms: I'm so sorry, your appointment can't go ahead as the specialist is ill. Could I book you for next Monday, or place you on our cancellation list?
Unfortunately the specialist is ill, so we must cancel. I can offer Monday of next week, or you could go on the list for earlier cancellations.
I'm very sorry to say your appointment is cancelled because the specialist is unwell. There's a place next Monday, or I can put your name down for a cancellation.
We've had to cancel your appointment because the specialist is unwell. I'm very sorry. I can offer you next Monday, or add you to a cancellation list.

quests.hint: Give the customer cost information before proceeding. It respects their right to decide.
quests.explanation: Telling the customer before work begins that the repair isn't covered and costs about 150 euros gives control back to them. Doing it beforehand avoids a much more difficult conversation later.
quests.situationText: As a technician, you find that a customer's repair isn't covered by the warranty and will cost about 150 euros. You phone before starting.
quests.sampleAnswer: Unfortunately, the repair isn't covered by the warranty, and it will cost about 150 euros. I wanted to tell you before we go ahead, so you can decide.
quests.correctAnswer: Unfortunately, the repair isn't covered by the warranty, and it'll cost about 150 euros. I wanted to tell you first, so you can decide whether to go ahead.
acceptedSynonyms: I'm afraid the warranty doesn't cover this repair, and the cost would be around 150 euros. I'm calling before we start so that it's your choice.
Unfortunately, the repair isn't covered by the warranty, and it'll cost about 150 euros. I wanted to tell you first, so you can decide whether to go ahead.
This isn't covered by the warranty, so it would cost roughly 150 euros. Would you like us to proceed, or would you rather think about it?
I've found that the warranty doesn't include this fault. The repair would be about 150 euros, and I'd like your approval before we continue.

quests.hint: Summarize each person's perspective neutrally and ask if you've represented them fairly. Accuracy builds trust.
quests.explanation: Stating both views in the same balanced language shows that neither person is favored. Asking 'Is that fair?' allows corrections and makes both people feel understood.
quests.situationText: Two colleagues, Anna and Luis, are in conflict about a decision. You're mediating, and you've listened to both.
quests.sampleAnswer: Let me see if I've understood both perspectives. Anna feels she wasn't consulted, and Luis feels there wasn't time to consult. Is that fair?
quests.correctAnswer: Let me check that I've understood both views. Anna feels she wasn't consulted, and Luis feels there wasn't enough time to consult. Is that fair?
acceptedSynonyms: Let me check that I've understood both views. Anna feels she wasn't consulted, and Luis feels there wasn't enough time to consult. Is that fair?
If I've got this right, Anna felt left out of the decision, while Luis felt the time was too short to involve her. Have I summed it up fairly?
I'd like to make sure I understand. Anna says she wasn't consulted, and Luis says there was no time. Is that accurate?
So, Anna, you felt you should have been asked, and Luis, you felt there wasn't time. Have I described that correctly?

quests.hint: Start from shared goals to reduce hostility. Then ask each person for their needs.
quests.explanation: Beginning with what both people want ('the project to succeed') creates common ground. Asking what each needs from the other turns blame into a request that can be answered.
quests.situationText: A discussion between two team members has become tense. You remind them of what they have in common, and you want them to look forward.
quests.sampleAnswer: There's a shared goal here, which is the project's success. What would help each of you work better with the other?
quests.correctAnswer: You both want this project to succeed, and that's a good place to start. What would each of you need from the other?
acceptedSynonyms: We all want the project to work, so let's begin there. What does each of you need from the other to make that happen?
There's a shared goal here, which is the project's success. What would help each of you work better with the other?
You both want this project to succeed, and that's a good place to start. What would each of you need from the other?
Let's start with what we agree on: we want the project to succeed. What does each of you need from the other?

quests.hint: End mediation with a small, specific, time-limited experiment. It's easier to accept than a permanent rule.
quests.explanation: A one-week trial is less threatening than a permanent change, and it includes obligations from both people. Scheduling a follow-up meeting ensures accountability.
quests.situationText: After a long discussion, you want the two colleagues to leave with a concrete plan. Communication is the main problem: one shares plans late, and the other responds slowly. The plan is due on Monday, with replies within a day.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm going to suggest a small step. For one week, you'll share the plan by Monday, and you'll respond within a day. Then we'll meet again.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to suggest a small step. For one week, you share the plan by Monday, and you respond within a day. Then we'll meet again.
acceptedSynonyms: I'd like to suggest a small step. For one week, you share the plan by Monday, and you respond within a day. Then we'll meet again.
Let's try something simple for a week. One of you sends the plan by Monday, and the other replies within a day. We'll review it afterwards.
Here's a small experiment: a plan by Monday, and a response within a day, for one week. Then we'll get together and see how it went.
How about a one-week trial? The plan comes out on Monday, and the reply comes within a day. We'll then meet to check.

quests.hint: Introduce yourself through what you do and what you're curious about. It invites conversation rather than only stating a title.
quests.explanation: Saying what you're curious about gives the other person an easy way to connect. Describing your work in terms of a goal ('reducing delivery times') is more memorable than a job title.
quests.situationText: At a professional networking event, a stranger asks what you do. You work in logistics, focused on delivery times.
quests.sampleAnswer: I work in logistics, mostly on reducing delivery times. I'm here because I'm curious how other people are using data for that.
quests.correctAnswer: I work in logistics, mainly on shortening delivery times. I'm here because I'm curious how others are using data for that.
acceptedSynonyms: I'm in logistics, focusing on making deliveries faster. I came along to hear how other people use data for it.
My work is in logistics, where I concentrate on reducing delivery times. I'm curious how others are using data in that area.
I work in logistics, mainly on shortening delivery times. I'm here because I'm curious how others are using data for that.
I work on delivery times in logistics. What brought me here is wanting to learn how other companies apply data to that.

quests.hint: Suggest a follow-up with a specific, low-effort format and a reason. 'Coffee' is easier to accept than 'a meeting'.
quests.explanation: Proposing a coffee next month is specific, relaxed, and time-limited. Linking it to your interest in their work makes the invitation sincere, not merely polite.
quests.situationText: At the end of a conversation with someone whose work you find interesting, you'd like to keep in touch.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've enjoyed talking. Could we meet for coffee next month? I'd like to learn more about your work.
quests.correctAnswer: It was great meeting you. Would you be open to a coffee next month? I'd love to hear more about what you do.
acceptedSynonyms: It was great meeting you. Would you be open to a coffee next month? I'd love to hear more about what you do.
I've enjoyed talking. Could we meet for coffee next month? I'd like to learn more about your work.
This has been really interesting. Would you be up for a coffee sometime next month?
Thank you for the chat. I'd love to continue it over coffee next month, if you're free.

quests.hint: A follow-up message should remind the person who you are, refer to the promise you made, and confirm the action.
quests.explanation: Reminding the person where you met and stating what you promised makes your message easy to place and builds a reputation for reliability. Confirming that the email has been sent gives a next step.
quests.situationText: You met someone at a conference on Thursday and promised to send an article. You leave a voice message for her. Your name is Ravi.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, this is Ravi. We met at the conference on Thursday. I said I'd send you that article, and I've just emailed it.
quests.correctAnswer: Hello, it's Ravi. We met at Thursday's conference. I promised to send you that article, and I've just emailed it to you.
acceptedSynonyms: Hi, Ravi here. We spoke at the conference on Thursday. I told you I'd send you the article, and it's in your inbox now.
Good afternoon. This is Ravi, from Thursday's conference. As promised, I've sent you the article by email.
Hello, it's Ravi. We met at Thursday's conference. I promised to send you that article, and I've just emailed it to you.
Hello, it's Ravi. We met at the conference on Thursday, and I said I'd send you that article. It's on its way.

quests.hint: Validate the tangent, park it, and give the reason for refocusing. A time limit is an honest reason.
quests.explanation: Saying you'd like to come back to the point shows respect, and mentioning the remaining time explains why you're changing the subject. It stops the topic from being dismissed.
quests.situationText: In a meeting with ten minutes left, a colleague is describing an interesting but unrelated idea, and the budget still needs to be discussed.
quests.sampleAnswer: Let's return to that another time. With only ten minutes remaining, we need to concentrate on the budget.
quests.correctAnswer: That's interesting, and I'd like to come back to it. For now, could we focus on the budget, as we have only ten minutes left?
acceptedSynonyms: It's a good idea, and I'd like to discuss it later. We have ten minutes left, so shall we deal with the budget first?
Let's return to that another time. With only ten minutes remaining, we need to concentrate on the budget.
That deserves a proper discussion. Could we park it for now and use the last ten minutes on the budget?
That's interesting, and I'd like to come back to it. For now, could we focus on the budget, as we have only ten minutes left?

quests.hint: Politely refuse to gossip, without judging the person who started it. Redirect to a work topic.
quests.explanation: Stating your own preference ('I'd rather not talk about her') avoids criticizing your colleague. Returning to the task provides a natural exit from the topic.
quests.situationText: During a lunch break, a coworker begins criticizing another colleague who isn't there. You don't want to take part.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'd rather not talk about her when she's not here. Shall we get back to the plan?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd rather not talk about her while she's not here. Shall we go back to the plan?
acceptedSynonyms: I don't feel comfortable discussing her behind her back. Can we return to the project?
I'd rather not talk about her while she's not here. Shall we go back to the plan?
Let's not talk about her when she can't respond. Shall we carry on with the plan?
I'd prefer to stay out of that. Could we get back to the schedule?

quests.hint: End a long call by interrupting politely, giving your reason, and moving to a summary of next steps.
quests.explanation: A polite interruption followed by a genuine constraint ('another commitment') is easier to accept than sudden silence. Summarizing next steps lets you leave with clarity.
quests.situationText: You're on a call with a client who keeps talking, and you have another commitment in five minutes. You need to end the call without being rude.
quests.sampleAnswer: Forgive me for interrupting. I must be somewhere in five minutes, so may we quickly agree on what happens next?
quests.correctAnswer: I'm sorry to interrupt, but I have another commitment in five minutes. Could we summarize the next steps?
acceptedSynonyms: Forgive me for interrupting. I must be somewhere in five minutes, so may we quickly agree on what happens next?
I'm afraid I have to leave the call soon. Could we recap the next steps before I go?
Sorry to break in, but I'm short of time. Could we confirm who does what next?
I'm sorry to interrupt, but I have another commitment in five minutes. Could we summarize the next steps?

quests.hint: Give a realistic probability and a way to reduce the risk. Confidence with limits is more trusted than certainty.
quests.explanation: Stating a probability ('seventy percent') expresses uncertainty precisely. Adding a risk-reduction step (a small test) turns a warning into a plan.
quests.situationText: Your manager asks if the new process will definitely work. You believe there's about a seventy percent chance, and a small test could reduce the risk.
quests.sampleAnswer: I can't promise it will work, but I'd put it at about seventy percent likely. We can reduce the risk by testing it on a small group first.
quests.correctAnswer: I can't promise it'll work, but I'd say it's about seventy percent likely. We could reduce the risk by testing with a small group first.
acceptedSynonyms: There's no guarantee. I estimate roughly a seventy percent chance, and a pilot with a small group would lower the risk.
I can't promise it'll work, but I'd say it's about seventy percent likely. We could reduce the risk by testing with a small group first.
I can't give a certain answer. It's around seventy percent likely to work, and testing it on a few people first would help.
I'd be misleading you if I promised success. My estimate is seventy percent, and a small trial would reduce the risk.

quests.hint: Missing information? Propose a provisional decision with a review date. The work keeps moving.
quests.explanation: A provisional decision allows action without pretending that the information is complete. Naming a review date ensures the decision is checked when the missing numbers arrive.
quests.situationText: A team needs to decide on a supplier, but a key report won't arrive until Friday. You want to avoid waiting or acting blindly.
quests.sampleAnswer: Since the data is incomplete, could we agree on a temporary choice and reassess on Friday?
quests.correctAnswer: The information isn't complete yet, so I suggest we make a provisional decision and review it on Friday when we have the numbers.
acceptedSynonyms: We don't have everything yet. Let's decide for now, and revisit it on Friday once the numbers arrive.
Since the data is incomplete, could we agree on a temporary choice and reassess on Friday?
We're missing some figures. I'd propose a provisional decision, with a review on Friday when the report is in.
The information isn't complete yet, so I suggest we make a provisional decision and review it on Friday when we have the numbers.

quests.hint: Explain a risk together with the backup plan. Include the cost of the backup so people can weigh it.
quests.explanation: Naming the risk and the backup makes planning concrete. Stating that the backup 'costs more but keeps the date' shows the trade-off clearly.
quests.situationText: A supplier may deliver late, which could delay your event. You have a backup supplier who is more expensive.
quests.sampleAnswer: We can't rule out a delay from the supplier. If it happens, we'll move to the backup, at a higher cost but on time.
quests.correctAnswer: There's a chance the supplier will be late. If that happens, we'll switch to our backup, which is more expensive but keeps to the date.
acceptedSynonyms: The supplier might be late. In that case we have a backup, which is pricier but would protect the date.
There's a chance the supplier will be late. If that happens, we'll switch to our backup, which is more expensive but keeps to the date.
We can't rule out a delay from the supplier. If it happens, we'll move to the backup, at a higher cost but on time.
There's a risk of a late delivery. Our plan B costs more, but it will still meet the date.

quests.hint: A farewell to colleagues should thank, mention what you've learned, and express the wish to stay in touch. Keep it sincere and short.
quests.explanation: Effective farewells name specific gratitude (support and learning) and end with an open door. Emotional speeches are best when short, because short words sound sincere.
quests.situationText: It's your last day at a company where you've worked for six years. Your colleagues have gathered, and you say a few words.
quests.sampleAnswer: It's been a privilege to work with you. Thank you for all you've taught me. I hope we'll stay in contact.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you all for everything. I've learned so much here, and I'm grateful for the support. I hope we stay in touch.
acceptedSynonyms: Thank you all for everything. I've learned so much here, and I'm grateful for the support. I hope we stay in touch.
I want to thank each of you. I've learned a great deal in these six years, and I appreciate your support. Let's keep in touch.
It's been a privilege to work with you. Thank you for all you've taught me. I hope we'll stay in contact.
Thank you for six wonderful years. I'm grateful for everything I've learned and for your kindness. Please stay in touch.

quests.hint: Thank a host with a reference to how they made you feel, and offer to return the hospitality.
quests.explanation: 'Made us feel so welcome' names the emotional effect of their hospitality. Inviting them to your home shows the relationship will continue and returns the kindness.
quests.situationText: You've spent a week staying with a friend's family overseas, and you're leaving tomorrow. You thank them at your last dinner.
quests.sampleAnswer: We can't thank you enough for having us. You made us feel completely at home. You must come and stay with us one day.
quests.correctAnswer: You've been wonderful hosts. Thank you for making us feel so welcome. Please come and visit us so we can return the favor.
acceptedSynonyms: We can't thank you enough for having us. You made us feel completely at home. You must come and stay with us one day.
It's been such a warm welcome. Thank you for everything, and please let us host you next time.
You've been wonderful hosts. Thank you for making us feel so welcome. Please come and visit us so we can return the favor.
Thank you for looking after us so well this week. You've been incredibly kind, and we'd love to welcome you at our place.

quests.hint: Close a meeting by summarizing decisions, promising minutes, and ending pleasantly. It gives everyone clarity.
quests.explanation: A short recap prevents different memories of what was decided, and promising notes 'today' ensures accountability. A friendly closing sentence lets the meeting end warmly.
quests.situationText: You're chairing a meeting that has run well. Three decisions were made, and it's time to close.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thanks, everyone. To recap, we've agreed on three things. I'll send the notes today. Have a good afternoon.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you, everyone. To recap, we've agreed on three points. I'll send round the notes today. Have a good afternoon.
acceptedSynonyms: Thank you, everyone. To recap, we've agreed on three points. I'll send round the notes today. Have a good afternoon.
That's all from me. We've made three decisions, and I'll email the minutes today. Enjoy the rest of your afternoon.
To sum up, we've settled three things. You'll have the notes from me by the end of today. Thanks, and have a good afternoon.
Let me close by recapping the three decisions. I'll circulate the notes today. Thank you all for your time.

quests.hint: Combine several requests into a coherent proposal: state the main intention, list the changes, and end with a compromise on the last point.
quests.explanation: A renewal request that lists specific changes ('rent, repainting, notice period') is a negotiation, not a complaint. Naming what stays the same, along with what changes, shows you're a serious tenant.
quests.situationText: Your lease is ending, and you'd like to stay another year. You'd like to keep the same rent, get the bedroom repainted, and shorten the notice period from three months to two.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'd be happy to renew. Could we discuss holding the rent at its current level, repainting the bedroom, and reducing the notice period to two months?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to renew for another year, with a few changes. Could the rent stay the same, could you repaint the bedroom, and could we agree on two months' notice rather than three?
acceptedSynonyms: I'm keen to stay another year. In return, I'd ask that the rent doesn't go up, that the bedroom gets repainted, and that the notice period is two months, not three.
I'd like to renew for another year, with a few changes. Could the rent stay the same, could you repaint the bedroom, and could we agree on two months' notice rather than three?
I'd like to extend my lease for a year, subject to three things: keeping the current rent, a repaint of the bedroom, and a shorter notice period of two months.
I'd be happy to renew. Could we discuss holding the rent at its current level, repainting the bedroom, and reducing the notice period to two months?

quests.hint: Raise a sensitive team-level concern by explaining your motivation, avoiding blame, and proposing a joint step.
quests.explanation: Introducing a sensitive topic ('I'd like to raise something') prepares the listener. Focusing on sustainability for the team, and proposing to look at priorities and staffing together, offers a collaborative path.
quests.situationText: Your team has been working long hours for months. You're not the manager, but you want to raise the workload issue with the department head.
quests.sampleAnswer: I want to bring up a delicate issue: I don't think the current workload is sustainable. Would it be possible to look at priorities and staffing together this week?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to raise something sensitive. I'm concerned the workload isn't sustainable for the team. Could we set aside time this week to look at priorities and staffing together?
acceptedSynonyms: There's something difficult I'd like to discuss. The team's workload worries me, and I don't think it can continue. Could we meet this week to review priorities and staffing?
I want to bring up a delicate issue: I don't think the current workload is sustainable. Would it be possible to look at priorities and staffing together this week?
May I raise a sensitive point? I'm worried about the sustainability of the team's workload. Could we find time this week to go over priorities and resourcing?
I'd like to raise something sensitive. I'm concerned the workload isn't sustainable for the team. Could we set aside time this week to look at priorities and staffing together?

quests.hint: Speak reflectively about your own progress. Use contrast (then and now) and end with what you learned. This is the language of a confident speaker.
quests.explanation: Describing a journey with a clear 'then and now' contrast is a powerful spoken structure. Ending with a reflection ('it was worth it') gives the story a satisfying close and reflects the whole course.
quests.situationText: A friend asks you how your English has changed since you first started to learn. You remember struggling to order a coffee, and today you lead meetings in English.
quests.sampleAnswer: I remember my first day, when I could hardly order a coffee. Now I'm leading meetings in English. It took a lot of practice, but it was worth it.
quests.correctAnswer: I remember when I could hardly order a coffee in English. Now I lead meetings in it. It took a lot of practice, but it was worth it.
acceptedSynonyms: At the start, even ordering a coffee was a struggle. Today I run meetings in English. It took years of practice, but I'm glad I kept going.
I remember when I could hardly order a coffee in English. Now I lead meetings in it. It took a lot of practice, but it was worth it.
It's strange to think that I once found ordering coffee difficult. Now I lead meetings in English. All that practice paid off.
When I began, I could barely order a coffee. Now I chair meetings in English, and I'm proud of how far I've come.
